direction.premise: Small physical cars and loose props share a toy driving playground without replacing the damage-focused driving game.
direction.composition: A third-person car and its nearby physical props fill the screen; a single joystick and small collapsible room control surround the world.
direction.shapeLanguage: The recovered GLB car has actual body, glass and wheel geometry, surrounded by cuboid and cylinder collision props.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Original toy-car body materials, animated wheels, head/rear lights and simple colored props preserve the source model presentation.
direction.paletteLogic: Colored cars and pale collision props stand apart from a dark striped ground; brake lamps remain red functional signals.
direction.typography: Small system labels name the room and solo state; the main world has no technical network debug overlay.
direction.signature: A driver pushes physical props in a common server-simulated playground while another driver sees the same objects and cars.
direction.distinction: FOG uses geographic orders and ZAMAZKA uses painted restoration fragments; this port retains its source game object and the specific input loop described here.

architecture.primaryVerb: Steer and accelerate a small model car with a joystick or keys, collide with physical props and optionally share the playground by room code.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Acceleration and braking change rigid-body velocity; steering turns the car, lamps react and the following camera settles behind it.
architecture.spatialRationale: A third-person car and its nearby physical props fill the screen; a single joystick and small collapsible room control surround the world. This keeps the current game object and its real inputs spatially connected on a phone.

production.renderer: Three.js retains the recovered GLB model and source lighting; Rapier 0.12 simulates the local or server-owned rigid-body playground.
production.focalAsset: NormalCar1.glb was recovered from the user’s Mini-car-3D repository; its model and materials are preserved in a local bundle.

motion.character: Acceleration and braking change rigid-body velocity; steering turns the car, lamps react and the following camera settles behind it.
motion.action: Steer and accelerate a small model car with a joystick or keys, collide with physical props and optionally share the playground by room code.
motion.anticipation: The current selection, room state and available control labels expose the pending operation before the player activates it.
motion.response: The next visible state responds to the actual control: A driver pushes physical props in a common server-simulated playground while another driver sees the same objects and cars.
motion.followThrough: The resulting world, board or round state remains visible until a later explicit action changes it; no decorative transition hides the outcome.
motion.interruption: Repeated input uses the current state; pointer cancellation releases held controls and hidden tabs stop transmitting held actions.
motion.reducedMotion: The complete play state remains legible without decorative entry animations; spatial gameplay and authoritative outcomes retain their original timing.

evidence.expectedChange: The compact room control expands with explicit create, join and offline driving choices above the active 3D playground.
